editorial:
Imagine sitting in on a cozy, private chat with some of the smartest people in animation history. That is exactly what you get here. You follow film critic Joel Siegel as he brings together a group of directors and producers to talk about the legends known as the Nine Old Men. These were the core animators who helped Walt Disney build his empire and create the magic we still love today. The vibe is very relaxed and feels more like a dinner party than a formal documentary. You get a real sense of the respect and love these artists had for their mentors, and it makes you feel like you are part of the inner circle.

What really works is how the movie balances old clips with heartfelt stories. The pacing is steady, and while it might feel a bit slow if you want high action, the personal stories make up for it. It is a great pick for anyone who loves the behind-the-scenes secrets of classic cartoons. To get the best experience, you should try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see the old sketches clearly. If you are a true movie buff, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing how the lessons from the Nine Old Men are still used in modern movies today. It ends with a montage of classic Disney scenes and final words of gratitude from the guests. There is no big twist since it is a tribute, but it concludes with the powerful idea that while the artists are gone, their creativity lives on in every new frame of animation.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Disney history and art.
